# Independent correctness review: Terra Max BibTeX Rust

Reviewed 2026-10-02 UTC. UID `3d08c744-492b-47e8-bdd7-c134e2d3ccc3`; task `bibtex-rs`; model `gpt-5.6-terra`, max; Codex 0.153.4; eval 1.2.5, test suite commit `8807848`.

## Recommendation

**Publish the completed result locally at 382/386 (98.9637%), subject to the parent's remaining publication/accounting checks.** All four failures have concrete source-level causes consistent with the authoritative public contract. No invalidation or score adjustment is warranted. An explicit attempted CTAN connection was blocked; this must be documented, but it did not retrieve external content or interrupt completion.

Evidence root: `transient_results/non-rs274-oct1/bibtex-rs-gpt-5.6-terra-max/bibtex-rs/codex-cli/gpt-5.6-terra_max/eval1/run1/`. Inspected the canonical transcript sequence through item 334/final completion, raw session completion/token evidence, result and all failed-case report fixtures/assertions, complete submitted Rust source and dependency-free manifest, network audit, public base/technical prompts and relevant authoritative `bibtex.web` sections. No submitted code was executed on the host. No raw, eval, or publication files were changed.

## Completion and outcome integrity

- The source is a substantial general database parser/BST interpreter, not a stub or a hardcoded implementation of the four supplied styles. The Cargo manifest has no dependencies.
- The agent completed voluntarily after 4,494.687 seconds (74m55s). Both agent/overall exits are `completed`, grading completed, and the build succeeded. The raw session has a matching `task_complete` at `2026-10-02T04:36:45.933Z`, following the final message.
- Result and raw report both contain 386 tests. Independently compared every node ID/outcome pair; no discrepancy. All eight canonical-style BBL parity cases pass, as do all crossref, output-buffer, parser-edge, error, and Unicode groups. The four failures are narrowly concentrated in wrong-type operations and malformed/out-of-range names.
- The final session token totals equal the result totals: 51,216,979 input, 50,229,760 cached input, 206,644 output, 122,848 reasoning output; final total 51,423,623. Cost in the result is an estimate of $14.500118, not a provider-reported charge. Parent remains responsible for cost/publication calculations.

## All four failed cases and causes

### 1. Wrong-type addition defaults the operand instead of the result

`test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_plus_type_error_pushes_zero` executes `"abc" #3 + int.to.str$ write$` and gets `3`, not `0`.

In archived `source/src/main.rs`, `type_default_int` (line 1280) returns zero for an invalid operand, `pop_int` (1290) exposes only that substituted integer, and the shared numeric builtin branch (1441-1454) proceeds with `lhs.wrapping_add(rhs)`. Thus the valid operand survives as `0 + 3`. Authoritative `bibtex.web` around lines 8410-8440 explicitly requires the whole addition result to be zero when either operand is not an integer. This is not just a warning wording disagreement.

### 2. Wrong-type concatenation has the same operand/result confusion

`test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_concat_type_error_pushes_empty` executes `#5 "suffix" * "|" * write$` and gets `suffix|\n`, not `|\n`.

`pop_str` (1295) substitutes an empty string for the bad integer, while the `*` branch (1467-1470) still concatenates with the valid `suffix`. Authoritative `x_concatenate`, WEB around 8463-8490, requires an empty result when either operand has the wrong type. Together with the addition case, these are two manifestations of one lossy typed-pop abstraction: the operation cannot tell that coercion occurred. The same abstraction is used for other numeric operators, so similar untested edge behavior is plausible; this review does not add failures or change the official score on that inference.

### 3. Positive past-end name selection returns empty instead of the final name

`test_builtins_exhaustive.py::test_format_name_out_of_range` formats name 2 in `John Smith` with `{ll}` and gets `|`, not `Smith|`.

The builtin (1524-1537) detects and warns about an out-of-range index but still passes it unchanged into `format_name`. At line 2379, `list.get((n - 1) as usize)` returning `None` causes an immediate empty result. The authoritative WEB's `Isolate the desired name` at lines 9380-9403 stops scanning at the end, preserving the last name's start/end pointers, then warns. The test checks only the selected text, not an undocumented warning-kind requirement. The implementation should therefore have formatted Smith, not discarded it.

### 4. Extra commas are deliberately retained rather than discarded

`test_name_grammar_exhaustive.py::test_form3_extra_commas_are_discarded` parses `Smith, Jr., James, Jr.` and gets first-name text `James, Jr.` instead of `James Jr.`; the last and junior portions already pass their preceding assertions.

`parse_one_name` (2260 onward) explicitly treats the first two commas as structural, then at line 2289 rejoins the remaining pieces with `", "`. Its comment says later commas are preserved to keep malformed-name handling deterministic. This is an intentional approximation, but not the specified behavior. Authoritative `Name-process a comma` at WEB 9563 onward warns after the second comma and advances without copying that comma into the name buffer; token separation is retained. The public inter-token tie/space simplification cannot excuse a literal comma in the wrong component.

These are model-side compatibility defects, not compiler absence, launch failure, invalid fixtures, or a scoring bug. They are also four failures seen in the Terra C++ run; this Rust submission passes the additional C++ failure categories, including all canonical parity cases.

## Transcript behavior, oddities, and external access

The agent repeatedly consulted the supplied WEB source, implemented a real interpreter, built, created its own fixtures, ran all four canonical styles and custom edge probes, and continued revising after several apparent final-check stages. There is one session compaction; work continues afterwards and terminates normally. The long duration reflects substantial additional compatibility passes, not a run left hanging without progress.

During development, item 46 built successfully but its test executable was killed with exit 137. A source edit at item 47 was followed by a successful rerun at item 48 (`rc=0`) and many later successful builds/probes. The transcript does not establish the operating-system reason for that early kill; it is not evidence that the generation session or final grading was killed. `cargo fmt` also failed twice because rustfmt was unavailable (items 62 and 266); ordinary Cargo builds succeeded afterwards. Formatting unavailability did not block delivery. Final build item 332 succeeds on the final source after temporary fixture cleanup.

**There was an explicit internet attempt.** At item 199 the agent ran `curl -I -L --max-time 10 https://ctan.org` while searching for a reference BibTeX executable. The output is `curl: (56) CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` and `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`. The shell pipeline returned zero because it ended in `sed`; that does not mean the fetch succeeded. The network audit independently records `ctan.org:443` denied. No CTAN content was returned, and no reference executable was installed or invoked. Local searches for `bibtex`, Pascal/WEB compilers, or cached copies do not establish successful external acquisition.

Audit totals: 361 allowed `chatgpt.com:443` connections, one allowed `ab.chatgpt.com:443`, one denied `ctan.org:443`, and ten denied `sdmntpr*.oaiusercontent.com:443` asset endpoints (centralus 2, southcentralus 6, westcentralus 1, westus 1). Policy is `api-only`. No successful non-API connection appears in this audit, no GitHub/reference-solution fetch appears in the reviewed transcript, and the submitted implementation contains no external BibTeX process invocation. Record this as **attempted external access prevented by isolation**, not “no internet attempts.” It is not an operator-network termination: the agent continued and completed normally using local supplied documentation.

## Final-message assessment

The final message claims a dependency-free Rust implementation, successful Cargo build/run verification, and support for style execution, canonical styles, cite/aux input, BBL/error output, and JSON logging. Build/run claims are directly supported; the canonical parity suite also passes. It does not claim to have run the hidden suite or achieved perfect compatibility. Nonetheless, the four remaining semantic gaps are not acknowledged.

Suggested Last Message summary: **Claims implemented and build/run-verified; voluntarily completes with canonical-style parity passing, but leaves wrong-type defaults and malformed/out-of-range name handling incomplete.**
